about.title: About Me
about.intro: Hi, I'm <1>Churui Huang</1>, a postgraduate student at Peking University pursuing a Master's degree in Smart City and Big Data. My research interests lie at the intersection of energy systems, transportation, urban computing, and spatial modeling.
about.paragraph1: My current research focuses on energy transition, renewable energy deployment, transportation decarbonization, and infrastructure planning. I am interested in how technologies, infrastructure, climate conditions, human mobility, and public policies interact across different cities and regions. By working with large-scale spatial, mobility, environmental, and energy data, I study the performance and spatial differences of urban and energy systems under different development and policy scenarios.
about.paragraph2: My work combines spatial analysis, optimization, energy and transportation system modeling, simulation, machine learning, and spatial intelligence. These methods allow me to examine urban systems at multiple spatial and temporal scales, from individual mobility trajectories and three-dimensional urban environments to regional infrastructure networks and global energy transitions. I hope to contribute to a better understanding of complex urban systems and to support more informed planning and decision-making.

items.title: A global feasibility gap in resilient island energy transitions
items.abstract: Island nations are central to achieving UN Sustainable Development Goal 7 on affordable and clean energy, yet the economic feasibility of their energy transitions has not been systematically quantified at the global scale. Using a high-resolution framework covering more than 1,800 inhabited islands and 50 million hourly records of demand and renewable potential, we assess the costs of resilient low-carbon systems. We find that over 50% of islands face unaffordable transition costs under current income levels, with burdens most acute in Southeast Asia, coastal Africa, and the Western Pacific. Incorporating climate-resilience design further worsens outcomes, reclassifying 7% of islands into higher-cost categories. Although continued technological progress is projected to reduce the global average Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) by about 4% by 2050, such a modest decline remains insufficient to bridge the feasibility gap for low-income islands, leaving substantial disparities in progress toward the energy equity objectives of SDG7. Our results highlight that market-driven cost declines alone cannot deliver affordable island transitions, calling for targeted international finance to bridge persistent feasibility gaps.

items.title: Carbon emission implications of toll discount policies and network expansions in highway
items.authors: Han Yang^†^, **Churui Huang**^†^, Qing Yu^*^, et al.
items.abstract: Highways account for a significant share of transportation-related CO2 emissions, yet policy interventions in mitigating these emissions remain underexplored. This paper investigates the impact of toll discount policies and network expansions on highway carbon emissions, drawing on long-term Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) data. We propose a bottom-up framework for estimating highway emissions and use a combination of time series decomposition and causal inference methods to isolate policy impacts. Our results reveal that toll discounts exert a significant and positive effect on highway carbon emissions, the shift of freight traffic onto highways reduces overall system-wide emissions: on average, each kilometer of discounted highway travel yields a net reduction of 52 g of CO2 per day in the transportation network. These findings underscore both the potential of policy-driven highway utilization to lower total carbon footprints and the importance of carefully calibrated policies to manage induced passenger travel.

items.title: Solar potential and deployment archetypes of electric vehicle integrated photovoltaics in urban fleets
items.authors: **Churui Huang**, Qing Yu^*^, Xuanyu Xu, Muze Zhang, Haoran Zhang
items.abstract: Vehicle-integrated photovoltaics can provide on-board solar generation for electric vehicles, but its urban potential is difficult to estimate because vehicle motion, building shadows, and operating regimes interact at fine spatiotemporal scales. This study develops a trajectory-coupled assessment framework that integrates three-dimensional building geometry, GPU-accelerated ray tracing, reanalysis meteorology, and real-world Global Positioning System trajectories to quantify photovoltaic generation and charging-demand displacement for 3,000 private electric vehicles, taxis, and buses in Shanghai. Results show that weather sets the seasonal generation envelope, while vehicle operation and urban morphology reshape realised output. Taxi generation is tightly coupled with daily irradiance (R² = 0.960), indicating a highly forecastable micro-generation profile. Explicit three-dimensional shadow modelling is essential: disabling building shadows overestimates annual generation by 24.4% for buses, 10.2% for private electric vehicles, and 2.9% for taxis. Annual gross generation reaches 5,093 kWh per bus, 558 kWh per taxi, and 381 kWh per private electric vehicle, corresponding to battery-side charging offsets of 4,482, 491, and 333 kWh yr⁻¹, respectively. However, fractional self-sufficiency follows the opposite order: private electric vehicles achieve the highest upper-bound ratio of 14.23%, compared with buses at 6.28% and taxis at 2.49%. These results reveal a structural decoupling between absolute energy offset and fractional self-sufficiency, suggesting differentiated deployment roles for vehicle-integrated photovoltaics across urban fleets.

items.title: An end-to-end open-source pipeline for 3D semantic gaze analysis in photogrammetric virtual reality
items.authors: Yao Yao, Yinghong Jiang, Qing Yu^*^, **Churui Huang**, Haoran Zhang
items.abstract: Behavioural research in immersive virtual reality (VR) increasingly relies on eye tracking integrated with head-mounted displays (HMDs), yet converting raw gaze streams into reproducible, scene-grounded semantic measures remains difficult, particularly in photogrammetric environments with dense and irregular geometry. We present an end-to-end open-source pipeline for three-dimensional semantic gaze analysis. The pipeline operates within a photogrammetric digital twin of an outdoor university campus and combines a weighted multi-ray visual cone, which integrates foveal and peripheral acuity into a single Effective Gaze Point (EGP), with a three-dimensional adaptation of the Identification-by-Dispersion-Threshold (I-DT) algorithm for fixation detection. Semantic labels are assigned by matching fixations to a manually annotated reference cloud of 3.3 million points using a KD-tree K-Nearest-Neighbours (KNN) procedure. We demonstrate the pipeline in a 30-participant case study involving free exploration, high-information wayfinding, and low-information wayfinding tasks. The resulting measures distinguish task-dependent gaze allocation: signage fixation share increased from 2.7% during free exploration to 7.7% during high-information wayfinding, whereas road-surface fixation share reached 44.2% under low-information wayfinding. End-to-end processing of the case-study dataset required 20.8 s on a single workstation. The pipeline provides a reproducible and extensible workflow for linking immersive VR eye tracking to semantically interpretable three-dimensional scene elements.
